title: Measurement Record
description: The fields a number carries before anyone trusts, reports, or acts on it. A speedup, latency, throughput, memory figure, or eval result is a claim about the world, and this is the shape that makes the claim checkable. Cited by APPEND_SYSTEM.md and skills/nuclear-review.

claim.shape: one sentence, with the direction and the subject
claim.example: Listing 10k rows dropped from 2400 ms to 410 ms.

baseline.shape: the number before the change, measured the same way, on the same machine
baseline.invalidWhen: the baseline is a remembered number, a published benchmark, or a different input

command.shape: the exact command that produced the number, rerunnable by a reviewer
command.invalidWhen: the command is not quoted, or needs unstated local state

environment.shape: machine, runtime version, dataset size, cache state, and whether the build is release
environment.invalidWhen: a debug build is compared to a release build, or an empty cache to a warm one

repeats.invalidWhen: n = 1, or the best run is reported and the rest are discarded

variance.shape: spread across runs, as a range or standard deviation, in the same unit as the claim
variance.invalidWhen: the effect is smaller than the spread, which makes the claim noise

measured.shape: what the instrument actually counted, in units
measured.invalidWhen: the metric is a proxy that includes work outside the change, or excludes the work the user feels

alternatives.shape: array of { explanation: string, ruledOutBy: string }
alternatives.invalidWhen: no other explanation was considered, so warmup, ordering, background load, and a different workload remain live

verdict.invalidWhen: the verdict is 'keep' while variance exceeds the effect

rules: A number that fails any required field is reported as unmeasured, not as a result.
Under 10 percent with n = 3 on a shared machine is noise until a rerun separates the runs.
An errored or timed-out run is excluded and counted, never silently dropped.
A perf claim that changes behavior also needs the run artifact required by APPEND_SYSTEM.md.
